thread:
alex: quick sync — ran the mixed FP8/INT8 KV cache shadow on prod-like infra, want to share odd tail-latency pattern i saw
maya: nice, drop numbers pls. which model and batch shape?
dinesh: is this the 30b decoder with streaming KV?
alex: yes 30b, seq_len=2048, avg request len ~120 tokens, concurrent streams ~48. shadow route used: FP8 for weights, INT8 for KV tensors (hybrid), prefix caching enabled
alex: microbench cmd i used: `bazel run //bench:kv_latency --model=30b --quant=fp8-kv-int8 --concurrency=48 --requests=20k`
ci-bot: shadow run started 2024-10-12T18:03:12Z, job id cb-4821
maya: raw p50/p95/p99 numbers? memory deltas?
alex: p50 6.1ms, p95 22.8ms, p99 78.3ms (baseline FP32-KV p99 was 41.6ms). memory per-gpu went down by ~1.2GB on average, but observed 2–3% CPU steal spikes
dinesh: interesting — p99 doubled. where is the spike coming from? kernel or memcpy?
alex: perf top shows increased time in `kv_dequantize` and `prefetch_worker` stalls. also more frequent KV eviction+refill cycles for long prefixes
sophie: could be due to quantization granularity — per-block vs per-tensor. we saw dequantizing many small blocks kills latency because it cannot be vectorized
omar: also check cross-stream cache contention. with hybrid KV we add an extra conversion path that is synchronized on cache-mgr mutex
maya: did you try batching the dequantize ops or moving to on-the-fly vectorized paths?
alex: quick patch: grouped dequantize into 64-key batches, re-ran small run: p99 improved to 49.7ms (still +19% vs fp32), memory saving remained ~1.1GB
dinesh: so grouping helps a lot. what's the CPU cost?
alex: CPU up ~6% during tail spikes, but amortized cost small. problem is cold-warm transitions: single stream hitting a cold prefix causes synchronous dequant + disk read fallback for some hosts
sophie: can we do async prefetch + speculative dequant? pre-dequant for top-k likely prefixes before the model requests them
omar: we can add a lightweight async dequant queue that the prefetcher populates; needs careful backpressure to avoid memory blowout
maya: operationally, will this change affect Dedicated customers? i.e., extra CPU might break their node SLOs
alex: plan: 1) add batched dequant path (safe opt), 2) prototype async pre-dequant in shadow, 3) run canary with reduced concurrency and telemetry flags to measure p99 and memory pressure
dinesh: +1. also include a metric for `kv_dequant_latency` and `kv_prefetch_backlog` in telemetry
sophie: add an eval for output fidelity on a 2000-example prompt set — ensure grouping/dequant doesn't alter logits beyond 1e-3 average KL
maya: timeline?
alex: i'll land batched dequant PR today (small refactor), run 200k request shadow tomorrow, CI bot will post artifacts
ci-bot: build passed: cb-4821-batched-dequant, artifacts: s3://redwood-shadow/cb-4821/results.tgz
alex: attaching sample diff snippet we applied:
```
// batch dequant path (pseudo)
for (chunk in chunks(keys, 64)) {
  read_quantized_block(chunk);
  dequantize_batch(chunk);
  write_to_kv_cache(chunk);
}
```
maya: great. any regression on output quality?
alex: initial fidelity: KL avg 0.0008 vs fp32, accuracy over eval prompts unchanged within noise. will run the longer eval
sophie: if async pre-dequant works we might get p99 down to ~42ms which is within SLA and still keep the memory win
omar: note: for on-prem customers with constrained CPUs we should expose a policy: prefer memory-savings or prefer tail-latency (config flag `kv.quant_policy`)
dinesh: also document fallback: if `kv.prefetch_backlog > 1000` disable async dequant to avoid thrash
maya: ok ops: create canary run for dedicated-nodes, add telemetry, gate by `kv.quant_policy`. ping infra for extra CPU margin for canary
alex: pinging infra and will post results here once shadow completes
sophie: thanks, this is a helpful reproduction. can someone add a short writeup to the experiment tracker? (brief notes + commands + CI artifact link)
alex: will add summary to the experiment doc: https://intranet/redwood/experiments/kv-hybrid-fp8-int8-1712349999
maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
summary: batched dequant reduces p99 tail significantly for hybrid FP8-int8 KV cache. memory savings ~1.1GB per GPU. plan: canary with async pre-dequant and telemetry, gate by kv.quant_policy. artifacts uploaded.
